title: Ageing with Purpose; Support for Caregivers
what_it_is: Ageing with Purpose; Support for Caregivers

sections.label: CPF retirement adequacy for seniors
sections.summary: It states CPF for older workers should gradually rise to younger workers' levels when economic conditions allow, and incentives can encourage deferred CPF LIFE withdrawals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Seven, we must continue to strengthen the retirement adequacy of our current and future seniors, including gradually raising the Central Provident Fund (CPF) for older workers to levels similar to that of younger workers, when the economic conditions allow for it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We can give better incentives so that seniors choose to defer their CPF LIFE withdrawals, giving them bigger future payouts and increased retirement adequacy.

sections.label: Papers and healthcare spending on ageing
sections.summary: It states eight Ministerial and White Papers and three PAP.SG position papers were tabled since 1984, and healthcare spending rose from over $4 billion to more than $10 billion yearly since 2011.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One, since 1984, eight Ministerial and White Papers as well as three PAP.SG position papers have been tabled, each calling for and dedicating significant resources to prepare Singapore for ageing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Two, since 2011, our healthcare spending increased by two-and-a-half times, from slightly over $4 billion to more than $10 billion a year, and it will continue to grow.

sections.label: 2015 Action Plan for Successful Ageing
sections.summary: It states $3 billion was set aside for the 2015 Action Plan for Successful Ageing, which calls for Singapore to be a Kampong and City of All Ages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Four, we have set aside $3 billion for the 2015 Action Plan for Successful Ageing, a plan remarkable for its ambition and scope, which calls for Singapore to be a Kampong and City of All Ages, with opportunities for our seniors.

sections.label: Older worker employment and support
sections.summary: It states Singapore ranks 11th among 35 OECD countries for older worker employment, supplements older low-wage workers' income through WIS, and raised retirement and re-employment ages to 62 and 67.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Today, we are ranked 11th among 35 Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) countries for employment of older workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We supplement the income of our older low-wage workers through the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We raised the retirement and re-employment ages to 62 and 67 respectively.

sections.label: Flexible work arrangements survey findings
sections.summary: It states MOM's Conditions of Employment survey shows firms offering at least one formal FWA rose to 53% from 50% in 2017, and ad hoc FWA to 84% from 75%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Manpower's (MOM's) recent Conditions of Employment survey shows firms offering at least one formal FWA increased to 53% from 50% in 2017 and firms offering at least one ad hoc FWA increased to 84% from 75% in 2017, which is a big increase.

sections.label: Food Panda riders above 60
sections.summary: It states that out of more than 6,000 riders Food Panda has today, only 1% is above the age of 60.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Yet, out of more than 6,000 riders that Food Panda has today, only 1% is above the age of 60.

sections.label: CPF rates for older workers
sections.summary: The Government can gradually raise employers' CPF contribution rates for workers over 55 to levels similar to younger workers when economic conditions allow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, the Government can gradually increase the employers' CPF contribution rates for older workers beyond age 55 to levels similar to that of younger workers when the economic conditions allow for it.

sections.label: MediSave and CPF LIFE support
sections.summary: It supports collecting MediSave contributions more seamlessly and encourages incentives for seniors to defer CPF LIFE withdrawals for bigger future payouts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, we support the recommendation by the Tripartite Work Group on SEP to collect MediSave contributions more seamlessly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Third, we encourage the Government to give better incentives so that seniors could choose to defer their CPF LIFE withdrawals, giving them bigger future payouts and increased retirement adequacy.

sections.label: Volunteers providing meals
sections.summary: Volunteers work with organisations to provide low-income families, including the elderly, meals 24/7, 365 days a year, with over 450 recipients now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Volunteers from there work with various organisations to provide low-income families, including the elderly, with meals 24/7, 365 days a year – let me stress again – 24/7, 365 meals a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As of now, they have more than 450 recipients receiving lunch and/or breakfast.

sections.label: Support services for seniors
sections.summary: Parents and students supplement these efforts, alongside free meal delivery, communal meals, a free medical clinic and stepped-up police patrols for frail seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: They are supplemented by parents and students from our local schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This is on top of what Community Network of Seniors and social workers do; (b) regular free meal delivery service through our partner Mummy Yummy; (c) regular, healthy, communal meals through the Health Promotion Board's (HPB's) Share-a-Pot programme; (d) comprehensive medical attention through our free medical clinic, which has the organisational and nursing support from Mount Alvenia Hospital; and (e) stepped-up patrol by the Police to the houses of the most frail seniors living alone.

sections.label: Cancer support network in Kebun Baru
sections.summary: For seniors with medical needs in Kebun Baru, a cancer support network was recently started so patients and families get information and peer support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For seniors with medical needs in Kebun Baru, we have recently started a cancer support network, so that cancer patients and their family can get the right information and peer support from their fellow residents, some of whom are cancer survivors themselves.

sections.label: Seniors and significant disability
sections.summary: Many seniors remain hale and hearty, but some have clear disabilities, with an estimated one in three Singaporeans suffering significant disability in their lifetime.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Many seniors, thankfully, are still hale and hearty, but some have clear disabilities, which is not surprising, as it has been estimated that as many as one in three Singaporeans will suffer a period of significant disability in their lifetime.

sections.label: Working caregivers and caregiving data
sections.summary: 2010 data shows close to three-quarters of caregivers work, and a 2013 survey found working caregivers took leave or went late for caregiving.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: According to the last available data on caregiving from the Department of Statistics, in 2010, close to three-quarters of our caregivers are working.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The 2013 Ministry of Community Development, Youth and Sports (MCYS) Survey on Informal Caregiving also found that for working caregivers, in the period of six months prior to the survey, 29%, or close to one-third, had to leave work at least once for the care recipient's doctor's appointment and 10% indicated that they went late to work over the same period for caregiving commitments.

sections.label: Legislating caregiver and eldercare leave
sections.summary: The passage proposes considering legislation for a certain number of days of paid and unpaid caregiver or eldercare leave.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: First, we can consider legislating a certain number of days for paid and unpaid caregiver or eldercare leave.

sections.label: More respite care facilities
sections.summary: It suggests investing in more respite care facilities in every housing estate, near Senior Activity or Residents' Centres, with pre-registration of essential details.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: While there is already a number of respite care services, both in-home and at day-care centres and nursing homes, I would like to suggest that we invest in more respite care facilities located strategically in every housing estate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Ideally, these centres should be located near Senior Activity or Residents' Centre and are, hence, both convenient and familiar to both care recipients and their families.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We should also consider allowing families to pre-register and list essential health, medical, financial and payment details so that in the event of an emergency or an urgency, such as a hospitalisation or perhaps an overseas work trip or holiday, families can place their seniors in these centres with peace of mind.

sections.label: Allowances for full-time family caregivers
sections.summary: The Government may consider providing allowances only to full-time family caregivers in lower-income groups caring for seniors with long-term disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Government may wish to consider providing allowances to only full-time family caregivers who are in the lower-income groups and who look after seniors with long-term disabilities, a more calibrated approach.

sections.label: One-stop information centres for caregivers
sections.summary: More one-stop information centres island-wide would help caregivers, especially those not computer literate or comfortable online, get reliable updated information.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Having more one-stop information centres at accessible locations island-wide would enable caregivers to obtain reliable and updated information more easily as not all of them are computer literate nor comfortable getting information online.

sections.label: ADL needs in 2010 and 2030
sections.summary: About 31,000 individuals needed help with one or more Activities of Daily Living in 2010, and about 83,000 in 2030 will have such deficits.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In 2010, there were about 31,000 individuals who needed help with one or more Activities of Daily Living (ADLs).

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: About 7% of the population or about 83,000 individuals in 2030 will have deficits in one or more ADLs.

sections.label: IDAPE eligibility and payouts
sections.summary: IDAPE eligibility requires three ADL deficits and pays about $150 to $250 monthly on a means test, which the passage calls insufficient.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Presently, the Interim Disability Assistance Programme for the Elderly's (IDAPE’s) eligibility is stringent with three ADL deficits requirement and the amount of about $150 to $250 per month on a means-test basis is insufficient.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The amount claimable of $300 to $400 for limited years is not sufficient for long-term care, as disability and frailty of seniors are usually not reversible.

sections.label: AGH care recipients and flats
sections.summary: AGH is looking after about 500 dependent care recipients in two precincts with 1,155 rental flats.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Presently, AGH is looking after about 500 dependent care recipients in these two precincts with 1,155 rental flats.

sections.label: Paid care leave for caregivers
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government will consider requiring employers to grant paid Care Leave to staff who are caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Will our Government consider requiring employers to grant paid "Care Leave" to their staff who are caregivers?

sections.label: Daily price range
sections.summary: Prices can range from $100 to $125 per day.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Prices can range from $100 to $125 per day.

sections.label: Caregivers Training Grant subsidy
sections.summary: Many caregivers get domestic helpers, but the Caregivers Training Grant annual subsidy is only $200 for each care recipient.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Many caregivers also get domestic helpers to assist them with their caregiving roles.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: But the Caregivers Training Grant annual subsidy is only $200 for each care recipient.

sections.label: Eldercare leave feasibility study
sections.summary: The passage states the Government is prepared to study the feasibility of eldercare leave to help working informal caregivers care for seniors at home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If they also work fulltime or parttime at a paying job, their performance suffers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We understand that the Government is prepared to study the feasibility of eldercare leave to help working informal caregivers also take care of seniors at home, as childcare leave helps working mothers.

sections.label: CPF top-ups for informal caregivers
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government would consider socio-economic support like CPF top-ups for full-time informal caregivers in low-income households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Would the Government also consider socio-economic support, such as CPF top-ups for full-time informal caregivers in low-income households, to reduce the pressure of being unemployed or underemployed and unprepared or underprepared for retirement or for old age as a result of taking on the responsibilities of caring for their loved seniors?

sections.label: Support for informal caregivers
sections.summary: Describes informal caregivers' low-paying or no work and lost CPF savings, and hopes for CPF top-ups and other financial support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These so-called "informal" caregivers are often forced to take up low-paying jobs with flexible hours and terms, or to leave the labour force altogether, thereby aggravating their low economic status in the family, and loss of opportunities to increase their CPF savings to meet future needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I understand that the Government is prepared to study the feasibility of eldercare leave to help working informal caregivers also take care of seniors at home, like how childcare leave helps working mothers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As for non-working informal caregivers who stay at home fulltime to look after the elderly, especially those from low-income families, I hope the Government will consider CPF top-ups and other means to provide them with financial support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Even as it is important to show support to our elderly in their golden years, it is equally important to care for the caregivers themselves because caregiving, though meaningful, can be extremely challenging and demanding on time, energy and emotion.

sections.label: Caregiver allowance provision
sections.summary: States that another way to support caregivers is to seriously consider providing a caregiver allowance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Another way in which we should support caregivers is to consider seriously the provision of a caregiver allowance.

sections.label: Caregiver allowance for the unhelped
sections.summary: Says caregiver allowance should be provided to benefit those who would otherwise not receive financial help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Because of the wide variety of ways in which care is provided, caregiver allowance should be provided so as to meaningfully benefit those who would otherwise not enjoy financial help rendered.

sections.label: Caregiver allowance and perceptions
sections.summary: Says providing caregiver allowance is a key step for the Government to lead a paradigm shift in perceptions of caregiving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Providing caregiver allowance will also be a key step that the Government can take to lead the paradigm shift in the perceptions surrounding the vocation of caregiving.

sections.label: Extending support beyond elderly
sections.summary: Asks that support for caregivers be extended to caregivers of the physically or mentally disabled or mentally challenged, beyond the elderly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It brings home, Mr Speaker, the importance of what we are debating through the two Private Members' Motions today in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Therefore, what I am asking for is that the support for caregivers be extended to caregivers of those who are physically or mentally disabled or mentally challenged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: But, surely, we can and should move beyond the elderly.

sections.label: Supporting vulnerable caregivers
sections.summary: It states that some caregivers are themselves vulnerable, including those caregiving alone or juggling work and caring for aged parents, and that helping them is especially important.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: When it comes to caring for caregivers, some caregivers are themselves in a vulnerable position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: They may be singlehandedly fulfilling caregiving duties, juggling between work during the day and caring for their aged parents at night.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It is especially important to help caregivers who are themselves in a vulnerable position.

sections.label: Meaningful senior years
sections.summary: It states that ageing with purpose and dignity requires spending senior years meaningfully, and estimates 900,000 Singaporeans, a quarter, will be seniors in a decade.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: To age with purpose and dignity, we must be able to spend our senior years meaningfully.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It is estimated that a quarter of Singaporeans, or 900,000, will be seniors in a decade.

sections.label: Extended family support policies
sections.summary: It proposes broadening the definition of family members in Government policies so extended family can help one another, including contributing to one another's accounts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: How about helping hands from extended family members?

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Therefore, we are proposing a broadening of the definition of family members in Government policies to better allow Singaporeans to help support their extended family members if they wish.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: If the extended family wishes to help, our policies should encourage it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We would like to suggest that extended members of a family be allowed to contribute to one another's account, for example, from grandchildren to grandparents, if they wish.

sections.label: Allowances and support for caregivers
sections.summary: It proposes a Government allowance for family or informal caregivers, especially full-time caregivers of elderly with disabilities or mental health problems, and more employer FWAs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Family caregivers are seldom compensated financially for their effort and time, and out-of-pocket expenses can lead to financial hardship for lower-income caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We would like to propose that the Government consider supporting family or informal caregivers with an allowance, particularly full-time caregivers taking care of elderly with disabilities or mental health problems.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For part-time caregivers who work, we appeal for more employers to offer FWAs so that they can retain talented and experienced staff who make valuable contributions to their companies and our economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We should also support our caregivers by forming a network of support and guiding them in the navigation of social space so as to better look after their loved ones and themselves.

sections.label: Seniors joining programmes
sections.summary: It calls for modifying programmes where possible so seniors can join in or contribute their talent, wisdom, experience and abilities, with family as the core.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Whenever possible, consider making modifications to programmes to enable our seniors to join in or, even better, tap upon their talent, wisdom, rich experience and abilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We want to have many helping hands in supporting ageing, with the family as the core, and the Government as well as other organisations in the community coming together to support our seniors.

sections.label: Grants helping elderly at work
sections.summary: It states that the WorkPro Job Redesign Grant, Age Management Grant, Special Employment Credit, Additional Special Employment Credit and WIS have alleviated some challenges the elderly face at work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The WorkPro Job Redesign Grant and Age Management Grant, the Special Employment Credit and Additional Special Employment Credit and WIS have helped to alleviate some challenges the elderly face at work.

sections.label: Sector-based approach for senior jobs
sections.summary: The speaker proposes a sector-based approach with consultancy services to guide employers in redesigning or creating suitable jobs for seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: There may be a need for a little handholding and a deeper understanding of the demands of the specific sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I, therefore, propose a sector-based approach with consultancy services where employers can be guided towards redesigning or creating suitable jobs for seniors that would benefit the business and the industry.

sections.label: Group and retirement homes support
sections.summary: MND or HDB and MOH could revise guidelines to promote private-sector group or retirement homes with AL facilities, and consider a public housing trial.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Ministry of National Development (MND) or HDB and MOH could support these efforts by revising guidelines to enable and promote the setting up of group homes or retirement homes with AL facilities in the private sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: On a related point, MND or HDB and MOH may want to consider doing a trial of the group homes for frail seniors in the public housing estates.

sections.label: Calls to review CHAS scheme
sections.summary: The speaker recalls sharing last year about frequent appeals to upgrade the blue CHAS card and calls for a review of the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In a previous speech earlier last year, I had shared about the frequent appeals I have seen for an upgrade to the blue CHAS card and called for a review of this scheme.

sections.label: Adjustments to CHAS subsidies
sections.summary: The speaker requests adjustments such as raising the income ceiling so more elderly residents qualify for CHAS, or increasing subsidies within the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The CHAS cards are very precious and meaningful for the seniors, and the scheme goes a long way in helping them with their expenses, especially for those who have to seek regular medical treatment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I would, therefore, request that some adjustments be made, for example, to raise the income ceiling, so that more elderly residents could qualify for CHAS, or to increase the subsidies available within the scheme.

sections.label: Resident seeking Senior Priority Scheme
sections.summary: A resident recently sought assistance to be eligible for the Senior Priority Scheme when applying for a 2-room flexi flat.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Recently, a resident sought assistance to be eligible for the Senior Priority Scheme in her application for a 2-room flexi flat.

sections.label: Reviewing schemes and caregiver support
sections.summary: The Government has implemented schemes like WorkPro Job Redesign Grant, Special Employment Credit and CHAS, with caregiver support, but assistance must be constantly reviewed with stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Government is aware of this situation and has already taken steps by implementing certain schemes like the WorkPro Job Redesign Grant, Special Employment Credit and CHAS that can help overcome several aspects of the challenges faced by seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: At the same time, assistance is also available to provide some kind of support to caregivers, like FDW levy concessions and the Work-Life Grant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, in order to ensure the effectiveness of all available schemes, we must constantly review the assistance rendered and continue to work with all stakeholders, for instance, employers, in order to keep on enhancing the support provided.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: (In English): I think there are many good policies in place to help support ageing with purpose and dignity and in providing support for caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is time though that we take a whole-of-Singapore, a whole-of-community approach to help ensure the implementation of such policies addresses the needs of those they are meant for and that the gaps are plugged.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I stand in support of the two Motions.

sections.label: Inter-Ministerial Committee for Ageing
sections.summary: An Inter-Ministerial Committee for Ageing was established in 1998 to manage ageing issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In managing ageing issues, an Inter-Ministerial Committee for Ageing was established in 1998.

sections.label: Elderly suicide cases and ageing study
sections.summary: Media reported 129 elderly suicide cases in 2017, the highest since 1991, and a call was made for a more comprehensive study.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In July 2018, the media reported that the year 2017 saw the highest number of suicide cases amongst the elderly aged 60 and above, which is 129 cases, ever since such cases were first tracked in 1991.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Ms Christine Wong, the Executive Director of the Samaritans of Singapore (SOS), stated that it is worrying that many seniors are turning to suicide as the only way to end their pain and suffering, when they should be enjoying the lustre of their golden years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The issues related to seniors that I have shared should be given the fullest attention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I hope that the Inter-Ministerial Committee on Ageing Issues can conduct a more comprehensive survey and study to obtain information and knowledge that will further improve and refine the current efforts so that our vision to achieve "Successful Ageing for Singapore" will become a reality.

sections.label: Arts for Ageing Well study
sections.summary: A 2016 NAC-commissioned NTU study found arts participation improves health, and an NUS study found it can slow dementia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Arts for Ageing Well study in 2016 was commissioned by the National Arts Council (NAC) and conducted by the Nanyang Technological University (NTU) School of Social Sciences found that participating in the arts or simply attending arts-related events can significantly increase mental and physical health.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The National University of Singapore (NUS) Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine discovered that by participating in the arts and community activities can slow down or even prevent the onset of dementia where, after a year of taking part in art, music and social activities, more than 20% of senior citizens surveyed saw an improvement in their memory.

sections.label: Fund beneficiaries since 2014
sections.summary: The fund has benefited more than 171 SSOs, 91 artists and some 8,300 beneficiaries since 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The fund has benefited more than 171 SSOs, 91 artists and some 8,300 beneficiaries since 2014.

sections.label: Cultural Medallion recipients
sections.summary: To date, 125 Singaporeans and Permanent Residents have been conferred the Cultural Medallion, Singapore's highest arts accolade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To date, 125 Singaporeans and Permanent Residents have been conferred the Cultural Medallion, Singapore's highest accolade in the arts.

sections.label: Annual festival senior beneficiaries
sections.summary: The annual festival has attracted and benefited close to 40,000 seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The annual festival has attracted and benefited close to 40,000 seniors.

sections.label: Esplanade senior performances 2017-2018
sections.summary: The Esplanade held close to 70 performances for seniors between 2017 and 2018, attracting 73,000 senior audience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Esplanade held close to 70 performances for seniors between 2017 and 2018, attracting 73,000 senior audience.

sections.label: Arts programmes for seniors
sections.summary: The Esplanade's Community Care Programme organised 200 arts events for 6,250 seniors and the Art Bus Programme brought 1,782 seniors to the National Gallery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Esplanade's Community Care Programme has organised 200 arts events for 6,250 seniors and brought many arts groups and artists to nursing homes, benefiting more than 900 seniors and patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The National Gallery and the Deutsche Bank jointly organised the Art Bus Programme to bring 1,782 seniors from 35 welfare homes to the Gallery, so that they have a chance to participate in arts activities and tours.

sections.label: Public healthcare expenditure doubled
sections.summary: Public healthcare expenditure more than doubled in the past six years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Public healthcare expenditure, for instance, more than doubled in the past six years.

sections.label: Financial support for caregiving expenses
sections.summary: The existing FDW Grant will be of little use, so providing financial support to offset caregiving expenses with autonomy will relieve the care burden.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The existing FDW Grant will be of little use to them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Hence, providing financial support specifically to offset caregiving expenses, whilst allowing the care recipient or his caregiver the autonomy to decide how to use the money, will be useful in relieving the care burden.

sections.label: More AIC-satellites in communities
sections.summary: More AIC-satellites should be considered within communities, perhaps co-located with Silver Generation Offices, SACs or Community Centres, so residents can walk in for help.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Beyond this, we should also consider establishing more AIC-satellites within communities, perhaps co-locating them with existing setups, such as the Silver Generation Offices, SACs or Community Centres (CCs), so that residents can simply walk in whenever they need help.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: An example is to make the Moments of Life app the digital equivalent of AIC.

sections.label: Respite care beyond working hours
sections.summary: If an elderly caregiver falls ill, no one may take over care duties at short notice, so respite care beyond conventional working hours will offer relief.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Worse, if the elderly caregiver unexpectedly falls ill, who will take over the care duties under short notice?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Therefore, providing respite care beyond the conventional working hours will offer relief and restore balance to the lives of these caregivers.

sections.label: Flexible work for caregivers
sections.summary: Enabling flexible work arrangements lets caregivers work offsite and deliver work while watching over the elderly at home.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: A more sustainable solution is to enable FWAs so that these caregivers can work offsite and continue to deliver work products while watching over the elderly at home.

sections.label: Incentives for employer flexible work
sections.summary: The Government could raise financial incentives, run a nationwide campaign and work with tripartite partners to nudge employers toward flexible work and output-based appraisals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: To enhance the appeal of implementing FWAs to employers, the Government could consider increasing financial incentives and mounting a nationwide campaign to solicit buy-in from employers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In addition, the Government could work with the tripartite partners and consider financial incentives to nudge employers to place more weightage on the quality of work output instead during appraisals.

sections.label: Support measures for caregivers
sections.summary: Four measures are proposed: subsidising elderly care expenses, consolidating care information, providing after-hours respite services, and encouraging employers to adopt flexible work arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: One, subsidise the expenses needed to take care of the elderly to help relieve their financial burden.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Two, consolidate information related to caring for the aged, put them up proactively in the community so that caregivers can get needed help in time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Three, provide respite services outside normal working hours so that caregivers of dementia patients can get enough rest and enjoy some work-life balance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Four, encourage employers to adopt FWAs so that employees who are caregivers can attend to family emergencies while still being able to complete their work.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model for caregivers
sections.summary: A Progressive Wage Model is recommended for professional caregivers, whose salaries are lower than in Australia, Hong Kong and Japan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: To incentivise more Singaporeans to consider caregiving as a career, I recommend introducing a Progressive Wage Model (PWM) for professional caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: According to studies, the salary of Singapore workers in this sector is lower, compared to other developed countries, such as Australia, Hong Kong and Japan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We have successfully rolled out PWM for several sectors now and I am of the view that it is time we extend PWM to the caregiving industry.

sections.label: Nursing home funding model
sections.summary: VWOs and social enterprises bid low for tenders, operators lose money, and the funding model may unravel as the population ages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As a result, VWOs and social enterprises like NTUC Health have to bid low to secure the tender.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Many operators are losing money and the VWOs have to regularly raise funds to cover the deficit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: With a rapidly ageing population and the need to increase the number of nursing home places in the years to come, the charity money may run dry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Losses will mount and the current funding model is likely to unravel at some point in time.

sections.label: Rethinking nursing home funding
sections.summary: The Government is urged to rethink how nursing homes are funded, noting the Pioneer Generation Package and the coming Merdeka Generation Package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Our seniors deserve better and I urge the Government to rethink the way we fund our nursing homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We introduced the Pioneer Generation Package in 2015, and we will soon launch the Merdeka Generation Package later this year.

sections.label: Goodlife!@Yishun fundraising golf tournament
sections.summary: A fundraising Golf Tournament raised half a million dollars to set up Goodlife!@Yishun as MOH lacked budget for renovation.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In fact, for this Goodlife!@Yishun, we did a fundraising Golf Tournament.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We raised half a million dollars to set up this Goodlife!@Yishun as MOH did not have the budget to support the renovation of this centre.

sections.label: Give and Take Café
sections.summary: In Nee Soon South, a VWO SASCO runs a café manned by seniors called Give and Take Café, next to Khatib MRT station.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In Nee Soon South, a VWO SASCO runs a café manned by seniors.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is called Give and Take Café and it is right next to Khatib Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) station.

sections.label: Free aromatherapy and hand massage
sections.summary: GoodLife@Yishun features Singapore's first free aromatherapy and hand massage service caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: GoodLife@Yishun also features Singapore's first free aromatherapy and hand massage service caregivers.

sections.label: Dementia go-to points in Nee Soon South
sections.summary: Schools, merchants and residents are being educated to recognise and help dementia patients, with dementia go-to points added including every RC in Nee Soon South.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Therefore, we are educating the schools, merchants, residents and so on in the area to recognise and help dementia patients.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We have added many dementia go-to points, including every RC in Nee Soon South.

sections.label: Seniors selling coffee at Goodlife!@Yishun
sections.summary: Selling coffee helps seniors earn extra money and share topics with young customers at Goodlife!@Yishun, managed by Montfort Care Centre.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Selling coffee can help these seniors earn some extra money and have common topics with young customers.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is located within Goodlife!@Yishun managed by Montfort Care Centre.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: When seniors come in for a free coffee, Montfort Care staff will have a chit-chat with them and invite them to take part in the activities.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Goodlife!@Yishun also features free aromatherapy and hand massage service for the elderly and caregivers.

sections.label: Waiving gross floor area charges
sections.summary: Some building owners cited additional gross floor area charges, so URA is called to review and waive them for a rest area space.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In our engagement with building owners, some shared that they are unable to do so because of additional gross floor area charges imposed on them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, I am calling for Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) to review and waive the gross floor area charges for a space specifically set aside to set up a rest area.

sections.label: Age management grant for employers
sections.summary: Employers can use an age management grant of up to $20,000 to implement age-friendly practices and assimilate older workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Employers can tap on the age management grant of up to $20,000 to implement good age-management practices, build age-friendly workplaces and assimilate their older workers within their organisations.

sections.label: Rest areas for elderly workers
sections.summary: Service buyers and building owners are urged to provide rest areas with tables, chairs, lockers and fans for workers including cleaning and security workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We must ensure that our elderly workers are able to take their breaks in a suitable environment so that they can perform their tasks properly after they had had their rest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I urge service buyers and building owners to provide a suitable rest area for all workers, including cleaning and security workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The allocated rest area should at least have tables, chairs, personal lockers and fans so that these elderly workers can take their breaks comfortably.

sections.label: Parents committing filicide
sections.summary: Some parents pushed to a corner end up committing filicide, the murder of one's own child.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Pushed to a corner, some parents end up committing filicide or the act of murder of one’s own child.

sections.label: Enabling Masterplan assurances for disabilities
sections.summary: The 3rd Enabling Masterplan must deliver better assurances and outcomes for persons with disabilities across early intervention, education, employment, financial security and healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I arrived at the conclusion that breakthroughs for these families can start only if caregivers are assured that their ageing children with disabilities will be taken care of.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Hence, the Enabling Masterplan for Persons with Disabilities developed under MSF, although comprehensive and impressive in presentation, is still not known by many in the community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The 3rd Enabling Masterplan (EMP3) must help deliver and communicate better assurances and outcomes for persons with disabilities in early intervention, education, employment, financial security, healthcare and other cross-cutting issues, such as end-of-life planning.

sections.label: Coordinated community support for caregivers
sections.summary: SG Enable's Caregiver Space is a good start, but a better coordinated web of local community support is needed for caregivers of persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The recent setting up of the physical SG Enable's (SGE's) Caregiver Space is a good start in engaging and training caregivers of PWDs and providing them with information and advisory services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As society rapidly ages and the demand for healthcare services and caregiving rises, there will never be enough manpower to perform the roles of caregiving and caregiver support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, we need to develop a much better coordinated web of local community support that includes neighbours, grassroots organisations, SSOs, corporate and individual volunteers that will support this unique group and their charges much more effectively.

sections.label: Strengthening support for caregivers of PWDs
sections.summary: Without a more systemic approach to strengthen this last mile, caregivers of persons with disabilities risk giving up or contemplating killing their children and themselves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The role of a caregiver of PWDs is even more so.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, unless we further strengthen and resource this last mile of execution, using a more systemic and systematic approach, caregivers of PWDs are at high risk of giving up and, in some cases, becoming so helpless and hopeless that they would even contemplate killing their own children first before taking their own lives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For a first-world country like ours, we must never let this happen.

sections.label: Elderly caregiver depression study
sections.summary: A Duke-NUS study found that one in five elderly caregivers suffer from depression.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One in five elderly caregivers suffer from depression, according to a study by Duke-NUS.

sections.label: Caregiving as labour force reason
sections.summary: The Labour Force Survey 2018 shows 88,800 people cite caregiving to families or relatives as their main reason for being out of the labour force.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Labour Force Survey 2018 shows that 75,800 women and 13,000 men, or a total of 88,800, cite caregiving to families/relatives as the main reason for being out of the labour force.

sections.label: Costs of caregiving and subsidies
sections.summary: Reports estimate home care for a severely disabled senior can cost up to $3,100 monthly, and note subsidy co-payment concerns and eligibility limits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The ElderShield Review Committee report estimated that, including transport, consumables and formal homecare services, it could cost caregivers as much as $3,100 per month to look after a severely disabled senior at home, well above the $2,400 median monthly fee for looking after severely-disabled residents in VWO-run nursing homes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The "Care Where You Are" report by the Lien Foundation notes that co-payment of care fees remains a key concern for families, although means-tested Government subsidies for long-term care have been increased to cover up to two-thirds of Singaporean households since 2012.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Even for those who are not severely disabled, daycare and homecare services can cost $900-$2,200 per month before subsidies, excluding transportation costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Families eligible for subsidies must co-pay between 20% and 70%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Those with a per capita monthly household income of more than $2,600 do not qualify for subsidies at all.

sections.label: Home-based care spending share
sections.summary: The Lien report noted Government spending on home-based and centre-based care was $240 million in 2016, 2.5% of the healthcare budget.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While the importance of enabling seniors to age at home is widely acknowledged, the Lien report also noted that Government spending on home-based and centre-based care, at $240 million in 2016, accounted for only 2.5% of the overall $9.8 billion healthcare budget for the year.

sections.label: Family care leave proposal
sections.summary: The Government should consider converting paid childcare leave into at least 10 days of family care leave so caregivers can keep working.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To enable caregivers to continue working while providing care, the Government should consider converting paid childcare leave into a longer quantum of family care leave of at least 10 days.

sections.label: Older resident employment rate rise
sections.summary: The employment rate for residents aged 55 and over rose from 57.2% in 2008 to 66.8% in 2018, attributed to a tight labour market, ageing population and declining birth rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: One, while the employment rate for older residents aged 55 and over rose from 57.2% in 2008 to 66.8% in 2018, this is attributed to a tight labour market coupled with an ageing population and declining birth rates.

sections.label: Retrenchments and PMETs
sections.summary: Retrenchments fell from 14,720 in 2017 to 11,020 in 2018, but PMETs remain more affected than other occupational groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Two, while the number of retrenchments declined in 2018, from 14,720 in 2017 to 11,020 in 2018, PMETs continue to be more affected by retrenchments, compared to the other occupational groups.

sections.label: Special Employment Credit ending
sections.summary: The Special Employment Credit is coming to an end on 31 December 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: One, the Special Employment Credit (SEC) is coming to an end on 31 December 2019.

sections.label: NTUC seeks SEC and CSP extensions
sections.summary: NTUC calls for a three-year SEC extension and a two-year CSP extension to boost older workers' employment prospects, especially PMETs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: NTUC is calling for a three-year extension of the SEC scheme and a two-year extension of the CSP to boost employment prospects of older workers, especially PMETs.

sections.label: WorkPro grants and extension
sections.summary: WorkPro grants support age management, job redesign and FWAs, but two grants end 30 June, so WorkPro ought to be extended and enhanced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Under WorkPro, companies can receive grants to support initiatives to implement age management practices via the Age Management Grant, redesign workplaces and processes to create easier, safer and smarter jobs for older workers under the Job Redesign Grant, and implement and sustain FWAs for all workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, the Age Management Grant and Job Redesign Grant will be coming to an end on 30 June this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The WorkPro programme ought to be extended and enhanced as we recognise the value of every worker and take steps to increase inclusivity of our workplaces to cater to a more age-diverse workforce.

sections.label: Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers
sections.summary: The Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers, set up last year, focuses on valuing older workers, retirement and re-employment ages, and CPF contribution rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers which was set up last year has been looking at the issues and concerns of our mature workers, focusing on four key areas: one, ensuring older workers are valued; two, reviewing the retirement and re-employment age; three, considering Singapore’s next moves on retirement and re-employment age; and four, examining CPF contribution rates for older workers and its impact on retirement adequacy.

sections.label: CPF contribution rate for senior workers
sections.summary: A Member supports the Motion and applauds PAP.SG's recommendation to keep the CPF contribution rate for workers aged 55 to 60 the same as those below 55.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: We cannot just stop at one level if we want to progress." I join my fellow Members of this House to support the Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I applaud PAP.SG's recommendation to keep the CPF contribution rate for senior workers aged 55 to 60 the same as those below 55.

sections.label: Extend Special Employment Credit
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Minister for Finance to extend the Special Employment Credit for older workers by three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: For that, I would like to urge the Minister for Finance to extend the Special Employment Credit (SEC) for older workers for another three years to cushion the impact of the higher CPF contribution by employers for older workers if that materialises.

sections.label: PA activities for elderly men
sections.summary: The speaker urges the PA to design activities that elderly men in the community would like to join.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And we are finding more of Mr Sharim and we are expanding the scope.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, for that matter, I would like to urge the PA to take a hard look and design activities that elderly men in the community would like to join.

sections.label: Tapping retired senior executives
sections.summary: A survey found most respondents keen to work after 62, and platforms like BoardMatch could tap retired senior executives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: An Economist Intelligence Unit survey commissioned by insurance company Prudential Singapore which was conducted recently in March 2018 found that most of those surveyed were still keen to work after the age of 62.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We could leverage existing platforms, like BoardMatch by the Centre for Non-Profit Leadership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: It matches senior executives with at least five years of management experience and leadership experiences from both the public and private sectors to the boards of non-profit organisations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Alternatively, an appropriate Government agency can take a lead in registering retired senior executives from the public and private sectors to better tap on their talents even during their golden years.

sections.label: Use of retired executives
sections.summary: The speaker says current activities struggle to draw men and retired senior management executives should be better used.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Current activities for elderly persons are having a tough time in drawing men.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Thirdly, we must make better use of retired senior management executives in the public or private sector, so that they can contribute more to the elderly.

sections.label: CPF Basic Retirement Sum
sections.summary: The CPF Advisory Panel's report noted that in 2013 only 55% of active CPF members met the Basic Retirement Sum at 55.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The CPF Advisory Panel's report noted that in 2013 only 55% of active CPF members were able to meet their Basic Retirement Sum at age 55.

sections.label: Integrate basic old-age payout
sections.summary: The speaker proposes formally integrating a basic old-age payout, a supplementary pension, with the CPF system.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To address insufficient retirement adequacy, especially among the elderly today, I propose that we formally integrate a basic old-age payout – call it a supplementary pension if you like – with the CPF system.

sections.label: Minimum retirement payout proposal
sections.summary: The speaker proposes a minimum retirement payout meeting basic needs, with the Government topping up CPF and replacing Silver Support and public assistance.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What I suggest is to combine Silver Support and public assistance for the aged with the CPF system by determining a minimum retirement payout that meets basic needs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government would commit to topping up the CPF retirement payout with this supplementary pension that replaces Silver Support and public assistance.

sections.label: Reasons for inadequate retirement savings
sections.summary: CPF decisions during working life affect retirement adequacy decades later, and three reasons are given why Singaporeans may fail to save enough.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the CPF system, decisions made during working life will have an accumulative impact on retirement adequacy decades later.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are three broad reasons why Singaporeans may fail to save enough for retirement: low contributions to CPF, low rates of return on investment and policy adjustments that have unintended effects on retirement adequacy.

sections.label: CPF tax credit proposal
sections.summary: Replacing tax relief with a tax credit would make the rich pay more tax, boost lower-income retirement adequacy, and pay for itself.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Eliminating the tax relief and replacing it with a tax credit would make the rich pay more in tax, but would give significant boosts to retirement adequacy for the lower-income, and it would also pay for itself.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I estimated recently that CPF tax relief costs the Treasury about $1 billion in foregone revenue annually.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If that foregone revenue were redirected into a system of CPF top-up credits, we could give all workers about $500 annually as a CPF credit.

sections.label: Lifetime Retirement Investment Scheme implementation
sections.summary: The speaker says the Lifetime Retirement Investment Scheme, recommended by the CPF Advisory Panel in 2015, must be seriously implemented.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Instead, we must look seriously at the implementation of the Lifetime Retirement Investment Scheme (LRIS), which was recommended by the CPF Advisory Panel in 2015, and which the Government has committed to implement.

sections.label: Retirement adequacy watchdog objective
sections.summary: A watchdog should assess how policy and socio-economic developments, including demographic change, immigration, labour market shifts and caregiving, affect retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The objective of this watchdog should be to assess the impact of policy and socio-economic developments on retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The projected effect of demographic change and immigration policy on housing prices and, hence, retirement adequacy, because of the potential excessive investment of CPF monies into housing.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The effect of the changing labour market, with increasing informalisation of work and disruption to traditional work arrangements, which, together with contribution rate changes, has a direct impact on the build-up of retirement assets.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The social insurance aspects of the system are also important, but other Members have expressed views there.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I will only note that many problems, such as inadequate support for caregivers and dependents, can be addressed within the CPF system itself, such as through granting CPF credits to those who contribute to our society in other ways than paid work.

sections.label: Seniors recruited and employed part-time
sections.summary: To date, 23 seniors have been recruited, trained and employed on a part-time basis.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: To date, 23 seniors have been recruited, trained and employed on a part-time basis.

sections.label: North West healthy living clubs
sections.summary: 315 North West healthy living clubs with 80,000 residents, 40% aged 50 and above, offer activities like brisk walking, dance fit, qigong, taichi, swimming and aerobics.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Presently, 315 North West healthy living clubs, representing 80,000 residents, of which 40% are aged 50 and above, have been set up, and activities include brisk walking, dance fit, qigong, taichi, swimming and aerobics.

sections.label: Dance Fit Club growth and fund proposal
sections.summary: The club grew from four clubs and 400 members in 2007 to 62 clubs and 3,500 members, and a Healthy Living Endowment Fund is proposed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: From a humble beginning of four clubs and 400 members in 2007, the club's membership has grown to 62 clubs and 3,500 members today.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: We are proud that 800 North West Dance Fit Club members will be forming a contingent to perform at this year's Chingay Parade.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: However, not many of these projects have been scaled up and implemented nationwide on a sustained basis to benefit all seniors in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In light of the above, I propose that Singapore should set up a Healthy Living Endowment Fund to support sustainable healthy living programmes.

sections.label: Social interaction, dementia and CIPC funding
sections.summary: A Japanese study linked greater social interaction to reduced dementia, prompting a call to review the CIPC funding cap for elderly-friendly amenities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In a study by Japanese researchers titled Social Interaction and Dementia Prevention: Six-Year Follow-Up Study, it was shown that "greater social interaction was positively related to reduced dementia".

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: A built environment conducive to active ageing will be of great value in encouraging social relationships and help to delay the onset of dementia in our elderly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: It is on this note that I call on the Government to consider reviewing the funding cap for Community Improvement Projects Committee (CIPC) projects for the elderly so that more elderly-friendly amenities can be provided to benefit our seniors in the community and give them the opportunity to lead dignified and happy lives.

sections.label: Singapore seniors by 2030
sections.summary: By 2030, one in four Singaporeans will be seniors, compared to one in eight in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In Singapore, it is said that by 2030, one in four Singaporeans will be seniors, compared to one in eight in 2015.

sections.label: European views of old age
sections.summary: A study found Europeans viewed people as old at 65, but researchers predict by 2050 people in their 60s will be considered middle-aged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The study found people across Europe were currently viewed as "old" when they hit 65.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, the researchers predict that by 2050 when people reach their 60s, they will be considered "middle-aged".

sections.label: Senior volunteerism and ageing population
sections.summary: Encouraging senior volunteerism promotes reciprocity and builds a caring, inclusive society, as one in four Singaporeans will be 65 or older in 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: From my observations, encouraging senior volunteerism will not just promote the values of reciprocity, but also build a caring and inclusive society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On harnessing wisdom, as mentioned earlier, 12 years from now, in 2030, one in four Singaporeans will be 65 or older.

sections.label: Caregiver platform functions
sections.summary: The platform could share caregiver information on training, subsidies and grants, and let caregivers view and make healthcare appointments for care recipients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The functions of this platform could include disseminating information relating to caregivers, for example, on caregiver training, subsidies and grants available for caregivers, and letting caregivers view and make healthcare appointments for their care recipients.

sections.label: Mother's stroke and bedridden state
sections.summary: Almost two decades ago, his mother suffered a stroke which left her bedridden.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Almost two decades ago, his mother suffered a stroke which left her bedridden.

sections.label: Security guard night job
sections.summary: He gave up his job and took a security guard job working 10.30 pm to 6.00 am while his mother slept.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: To be able to do this, he gave up his job, took up a security guard job that allowed him to work from 10.30 pm to 6.00 am when his mother was sleeping.

sections.label: Family love and no bedsores
sections.summary: He believes only family love will ensure his mother lives as long as possible, and is proud she had no bedsores in 18 bedridden years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For him, it is clear in his mind that only love from the family will ensure that his mother will live as long as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: He is very proud of the fact that his mother did not suffer bedsores despite being bedridden for 18 years.

sections.label: Mother's death at 86
sections.summary: His mother passed away a few months ago at the age of 86.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: His mother passed away a few months ago at the age of 86.

sections.label: Community resources for Mr Noorman
sections.summary: Community resources provided Mr Noorman legal assistance to be his mother's deputy, financial assistance, medical supplies, and hospital beds for caregivers lifting bedridden family members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For example, in relation to Mr Noorman, through community resources, we provided him with legal assistance to be appointed as his mother's deputy by the Court, financial assistance and medical supplies using resources from the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: We also made available a number of hospital beds to caregivers to help them with the physical task of lifting their bedridden family members for activities, such as feeding, getting them out of bed and so forth.

sections.label: Government help for seniors caregivers
sections.summary: The Government can help by identifying seniors and caregivers, getting their consent and linking them to community programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: And it is also an enormous commitment on the time of these volunteers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This is where I feel that the Government can help through identifying seniors and caregivers, getting their consent and providing the linkage to community programmes.

sections.label: Healthcare expenditure and caregiver support tradeoffs
sections.summary: Healthcare expenditure has risen two-and-a-half times since 2011 to over $10 billion, so financial tradeoffs in supporting caregivers must be understood.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The point to note is that our expenditure on healthcare is already up, as mentioned by Mr Henry Kwek.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It has increased two-and-a-half times since 2011 to more than $10 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: So, we need to understand what are the implications, what are the financial tradeoffs in deciding how much Government resources should be used to provide support for caregivers, bearing in mind their relative size to the population of Singapore and other needs.

sections.label: LPA and Will writing service
sections.summary: One proposal is service provision of Lasting Power of Attorney and Will writing for HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: One, service provision of Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) and Will writing for HDB flats.

sections.label: Common service for senior home owners
sections.summary: MND is asked to consider a common service for senior home owners to sign up for LPA and Will writing for their HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: How and who best can make appropriate decisions for them at that point of time?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: It is with this thought that I am asking MND to consider the provision of a common service for senior home owners to sign up for LPA and also Will writing specifically related to their HDB flats.

sections.label: CPF cap for short-lease property
sections.summary: There is currently a cap on the maximum CPF savings usable to buy a property with a lease under 60 years.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: First, there is currently a cap on the maximum amount of CPF savings that can be used for the purchase of a property with a lease that is less than 60 years.

sections.label: Review of RA top-up after LBS
sections.summary: The requirement to top up one's RA based on the age-adjusted Basic Retirement Sum after the Lease Buyback Scheme needs review.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Second, the requirement to top up one's RA based on the current age-adjusted Basic Retirement Sum (BRS) after signing up for the Lease Buyback Scheme (LBS) needs to be reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Some seniors have expressed why they prefer not to take up the scheme as they found that they remain "cash poor" after selling the lease to HDB.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: With time, the BRS continues to be adjusted upwards and there will be a point when there are little cash proceeds from the scheme unless substantial savings already exist in one's CPF.

sections.label: Seniors needing housing flexibility
sections.summary: The passage lists three groups of seniors for whom more can be done, including those mentally challenged, forsaken by family, or terminally ill.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: But there is always more that can be done.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: They include: (a) seniors with mentally challenged conditions and unable to live with another unrelated person in the same flat; (b) seniors who are not officially divorced but have been forsaken by their family; and (c) seniors who are diagnosed with terminal or multiple chronic illnesses and wish to cash out from their existing flat and use the monies towards medical treatment.

sections.label: Elderly transport in private estates
sections.summary: The passage urges the Government to work with the private sector on innovative transport for elderly living in less accessible private estates.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: To help reduce their future transport cost and to encourage greater mobility amongst older seniors, I urge the Government to work with the private sector to begin planning and developing various forms of innovative transport service for the elderly living at less accessible locations within the private estates.

sections.label: Singapore ageing demographic statistics
sections.summary: The passage states that by 2030, 27% of Singapore's population will be 65 and older, and cites the 1970s Old-Age Support Ratio of 13.5.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Singapore is experiencing a similar situation, In fact, we could be facing what some people have referred to as a "demographic timebomb" as, by the year 2030, 27% of our population will be 65 and older.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the 1970s, Singapore's Old-Age Support Ratio was 13.5, that is, there were 13.5 working age adults supporting every elderly person above 65.

sections.label: Health and disability by 65
sections.summary: The passage says it is critical for Singaporeans to remain healthy, citing MOH statistics that one in two could suffer disability by 65.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is, therefore, critical that Singaporeans continue to remain healthy so that they can experience the joy of their post-retirement silver years with their loved ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It was a wake-up call for many people when MOH released the statistics that one in two Singaporeans could suffer from some form of disability by the time they reach 65.

sections.label: Early healthy foundation for later years
sections.summary: The passage states that a healthy foundation laid early determines later health, and urges a whole-of-Government approach for citizens aged 40 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And I firmly believe that it is this healthy foundation that is laid early on in one's life that will determine one's health and physical wellness in one's later years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would urge the Government to adopt a whole-of-Government approach to encourage citizens, especially those 40 and above, for example.

sections.label: Agencies promoting healthier living
sections.summary: The passage proposes AVA or SFA and HPB mandate sugar levels, MOH and polyclinics offer subsidised screening, and SGActive set aside discounted senior hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: AVA or SFA, and HPB could jointly mandate the level of sugar in processed food and promote the use of healthier cooking methods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: MOH and the network of polyclinics could offer subsidised health screening for those aged 40 and above, and SGActive could set aside dedicated hours for senior citizens to use their facilities at discounted rates to promote the take-up of exercise.

sections.label: Seniors learning technology at libraries
sections.summary: Asks whether NLB and PA would work with Institutes of Higher Learning to set up booths helping seniors with IT at libraries and Community Centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To encourage senior citizens to venture into the world of technology and to make better use their smart devices, would organisations like the National Library Board (NLB) and PA consider working with Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs), such as the Institutes of Technical Education (ITEs), polytechnics and universities, to set up booths at libraries and Community Centres (CCs) to help the elderlies with IT-related matters and to teach them how to stay connected through technology?

sections.label: Smart devices for seniors
sections.summary: Says basic smart devices could be offered at a nominal rate to seniors above 60, and free for those facing financial difficulties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
